newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goh family takes major stake in Rebel Sport.
newsitem.headline: Goh family takes major stake in Rebel Sport.

text.p: The Goh brothers of Singapore on Wednesday made their first foray into the competitive Australian retail market with a A$12.7 million investment in sporting goods retailer Rebel Sport Ltd.
George Goh, the chairman of retail group World of Sports which has more than 50 stores mainly in Southeast Asia, said the two companies should now become a major retailing force in the Asian region.
With their 19.9 percent stake, the Goh family is now the largest shareholder in Rebel which has 26 stores in Australia and New Zealand and about seven percent of the Australian sporting goods market.
Rebel also has ambitious growth plans which include the opening of four stores each in Australia and New Zealand this year and a possible doubling of revenue before the year 2000.
By this time, the company hopes it could have 45 Australian stores compared with 23 currently.
The investment ends six months of negotiations which began with George Goh first offering to buy the 19.9 percent stake from Rebel's founding shareholder and non-executive chairman Sam Linz.

Encouraged by this offer, Rebel hired an investment bank to see if the company could be sold outright but returned to the negotiating table with the Goh brothers after a satisfactory full bid in the range fo A$2.00 per share did not emerge.
Major retailers which held tentative talks with Rebel included Coles Myer Ltd and its keen rival David Jones Ltd.

In today's deal, the Goh brothers paid A$1.65 per share for the bulk of the stake held by Linz with a further eight percent stake acquired by Rebel's joint managing directors Ian Dresner and Hilton Seskin, which increased their combined holding to 18 percent.

"I think one day we can be a very great company because these two gentlemen (Dresner and Seskin) they are full of fire like the Goh brothers," George Goh said at a news conference to announce the deal.

The three brothers, twins George and Joe along with younger brother Steven, are controlling shareholders in sporting goods, apparel and property firm Ossia International Ltd which listed on the mainboard of the Singapore Stock Exchange in Novembr 1996.
George Goh said World of Sports, which has stores in Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, and Taiwan, was a privately-held family group unrelated to Ossia.
Rebel shares, which spiked five cents higher on news of the Goh family deal mid-morning, were steady at A$1.65 in afternoon trade.
Dresner said he hoped the Goh investment would be a positive for the share price which had been under pressure due to the six months of speculation about what would happen to the Linz stake.
